findings.text: Tokdash 是独立的本地用量与费用看板，适合需要按工具、模型或会话回顾AI编码使用情况的人。DSH输入来自会话事件日志，DSHParser实际调用共享解码和用量折叠模块，再把输入、输出、缓存用量及模型映射成条目，并由价格库计算估算费用。相比人工逐份翻日志或把所有usage事件直接相加，它提供统一条目与界面；日志本身的用量记录仍来自宿主，价格来自本地数据库，不是从供应商账单取回的实际扣费。合格结果应是与一组可核对日志的计数一致，而不是看到图表即视为财务准确。
[Q02](#research-q02) DSH日志按尝试折叠，重复样本覆盖并跨物理副本去重，最后按价格库估算费用。
检查DSH解析、共享折叠、价格计算与API局部写保护，未覆盖全部来源、远程更新认证或整个看板安全面。
独立Python本地看板，不是DSH注入插件；pyproject声明2.7.1。

| 依赖或条件 | 是否必需 | 用途 | 缺失或不满足时 |

| Python>=3.10及包依赖 | 必需 | 服务与解码 | 不能按声明运行 |
| 可读且受支持的宿主日志 | 统计必需 | 提取用量 | 跳过或记录诊断，不当零使用 |
| 正确的模型价格映射 | 金额解释必需 | 计算估算成本 | 不用金额作扣费结论 |
| 本地受控网络入口 | 本地试用条件 | 保护用量与会话信息 | 不扩大到未验收远程暴露 |

| 阶段 | 现金与资源成本 | 人工与时间投入 | 已知条件与未知项 |
|---|---|---|---|
| 首次使用 | 本机扫描与存储量未知 | 配路径、核对样本耗时未知 | 需可读会话日志 |
| 持续使用 | 缓存、服务CPU与内存未测 | 维护价格与格式映射 | 金额不是实际账单 |
| 失败恢复 | 重解析资源未知 | 检查坏帧、缺失模型和诊断 | 缺失原始行无法靠缓存复原 |
| 退出 | 派生数据备份空间未知 | 停服务、保留原日志 | 远程入口需另行收回 |

|---|---|---|
| DSH计数 | 按尝试折叠并跨副本去重 | 全部宿主版本及真实日志完整率 |
| 金额回顾 | 使用本地价格计算 | 实际扣费、节时与财务准确性 |
[Q02](#research-q02) 共用解码、稳定条目键和版本化解析签名防止视图口径漂移；将价格与内容身份作为一个快照发布的方式可复用，但大源解析模块和宿主格式适配会带来维护负担。
[Q01](#research-q01) 和[Q02](#research-q02) 将异构工具日志归一并处理DSH重试、压缩和副本，贡献在计数语义和使用回顾；宿主用量与价格来源不归本工具原创。

[Q04](#research-q04) 给总计附带来源和价格覆盖状态，可能降低把缺失当作零费用的误判；需用户任务对照验证。

technical.rationale: [Q02](#research-q02) 相对简单累加，重试/压缩/副本一致语义为机制实质15、可迁移10；并非新日志协议，新意9、组合简化4。

business.rationale: [Q01](#research-q01) 统一回顾改变人工汇总流程取18；报告交付8、个人触达5为小幅，未证实预算或商业结构变化经济0。

recommendation.reason: 保存 DSH 会话日志并愿意核对计数的个人开发者可试用本地 Tokdash 回顾用量。相比人工翻日志，它按会话与模型汇总，并显式处理重试和重复文件，但金额仍是本地价格估算。日志格式被跳过、模型价格缺失或样本不一致时，应暂停费用判断并回到原始日志和供应商账单。

核心贡献 [Q01](#research-q01) 和[Q02](#research-q02) 将异构工具日志归一并处理DSH重试、压缩和副本，贡献在计数语义和使用回顾；宿主用量与价格来源不归本工具原创。 ## 关键质疑 [Q03](#research-q03) 缺失帧无法还原，未知价格计算可返回零，图表金额因此不等于实际账单，必须核对覆盖和模型映射。 ## 重点创新推演与最小验证 [Q04](#research-q04) 给总计附带来源和价格覆盖状态，可能降低把缺失当作零费用的误判；需用户任务对照验证。 未执行目标代码、安装或测试，无真实账单和宿主验收。后续固定日志核对不等同于已完成。 ## 研究问题与完整回答 **插件研究总目标**：Tokdash 的 DSH 日志统计能否支持可解释的个人使用回顾？ ### Q01 · Tokdash 怎样把 DSH 使用日志变成可比较的本地统计？ **研究主题**：场景与需求、贡献与相对优势、功能与机制 #### 完整回答 Tokdash 是独立的本地用量与费用看板，适合需要按工具、模型或会话回顾AI编码使用情况的人。DSH输入来自会话事件日志，DSHParser实际调用共享解码和用量折叠模块，再把输入、输出、缓存用量及模型映射成条目，并由价格库计算估算费用。相比人工逐份翻日志或把所有usage事件直接相加，它提供统一条目与界面；日志本身的用量记录仍来自宿主，价格来自本地数据库，不是从供应商账单取回的实际扣费。合格结果应是与一组可核对日志的计数一致，而不是看到图表即视为财务准确。 #### 证据与依据 **依据 1 · 作者声明**：[README.md:107-112](https://github.com/JingbiaoMei/Tokdash/blob/f0868fe1b745a4d13eacc63dc479edb29e238f8e/README.md#L107-L112) 作者将其定位为本地FastAPI看板 ```text ### WebUI The dashboard is a single page served by the local FastAPI app: exact input / cache / output token breakdowns, per-tool and per-model tables, a contribution heatmap, a week/month/year **Report**, per-provider **Quota** windows with reset countdowns, and a **Servers** tab that combines and compares several machines. ``` **依据 2 · 源码核查**：[src/tokdash/sources/coding_tools.py:5961-5999](https://github.com/JingbiaoMei/Tokdash/blob/f0868fe1b745a4d13eacc63dc479edb29e238f8e/src/tokdash/sources/coding_tools.py#L5961-L5999) 实际将折叠样本映射成统计条目并调用价格库
查看原文（39行） ```text def _entries_for_decoded(self, path_str: str, decoded: Any) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]: """Fold one decoded log into usage entries. Shared by the live ``_parse_all`` and the stored ``_parse_file_strict`` so the two surfaces can never bill one file differently. """ session_id = str(decoded.header.get("id") or Path(path_str).parent.name) entries: List[Dict[str, Any]] = [] for sample in fold_dsh_usage_samples(decoded.header, decoded.events): model = sample["model"] input_t = sample["input"] output_t = sample["output"] cache_r = sample["cache_read"] cache_w = sample["cache_write"] entries.append( { "source": self.source_name, "model": model, "provider": sample["provider"], "input": input_t, "output": output_t, "cacheRead": cache_r, "cacheWrite": cache_w, "reasoning": 0, "cost": self.pricing_db.get_cost(model, input_t, output_t, cache_r, cache_w), "timestamp": int(sample["timestamp_ms"]), "entry_id": dsh_sample_entry_id(session_id, sample), "_session_id": session_id, **({"_speed": sample["_speed"]} if "_speed" in sample else {}), "_billing": usage_billing_pricing( [model], input_tokens=input_t, output_tokens=output_t, cache_read=cache_r, cache_write=cache_w, ), } ) return entries ```
### Q02 · 重试、重复文件和损坏日志怎样影响计数可信度？ **研究主题**：功能与机制、工程质量与复用、缺陷与关键质疑 #### 完整回答 固定实现不是简单累加每一事件。折叠器在每个turn、step下推进retry-started的attempt序号，同一attempt的后续样本覆盖此前样本，并把压缩调用按时间另行记账；这样可以避免chunk与最终消息重复，同时保留重试开销。DSHParser又按稳定entry_id在重复物理文件间选最早位置，存储解析遇到无法读取的文件则抛专用异常，避免把读失败当作空文件删除历史。支持的格式代际固定为0、3、4；损坏压缩帧可跳过并报告，但跳过的行无法恢复，seed边界无法证明时不计费而非猜测。这些机制提高可解释性，却不证明任何新宿主格式、损坏日志或重复样本都得到完整账单。缓存签名包含解码/计数版本，价格状态与其内容签名原子发布的做法可借鉴；本次没有运行这些恢复或缓存用例。 #### 证据与依据 **依据 1 · 源码核查**：[src/tokdash/sources/dsh_log.py:45-58](https://github.com/JingbiaoMei/Tokdash/blob/f0868fe1b745a4d13eacc63dc479edb29e238f8e/src/tokdash/sources/dsh_log.py#L45-L58) 支持格式范围
查看原文（14行） ```text # Format generations Tokdash reads. A version outside this set is unsupported, # not corrupt — the file is skipped, never treated as empty. # # 0 is the developer-preview layout. 4 is what dsh >= 0.2.0 writes # (SESSION_FORMAT_VERSION in @deepseek-ai/dsh-session); its usage events keep # the v0 shape (assistant/message with data.turn/step/data.usage), so the fold # reads both. dsh names those files session.v4.jsonl[.zstd]; discovery matches # them on the suffix. 3 is what earlier dsh builds left on disk: its # header has the v4 key set, and dsh's own v3 reader cuts a seeded log at the # final inherited end-seed marker exactly as v4 does, so the same fold and seed # boundary apply (a real 24-log v3/v4 corpus decoded whole, #147). Generations # 1-2 were superseded in place upstream and are not claimed here until a corpus # proves the read. SUPPORTED_SESSION_FORMAT_VERSIONS = frozenset({0, 3, 4}) ```
**依据 2 · 源码核查**：[src/tokdash/sources/dsh_log.py:163-190](https://github.com/JingbiaoMei/Tokdash/blob/f0868fe1b745a4d13eacc63dc479edb29e238f8e/src/tokdash/sources/dsh_log.py#L163-L190) 帧损失与无法证明seed的告警
查看原文（28行） ```text def report_dsh_decode(path: Any, decoded: "DSHDecodedSession") -> None: """Report everything one decode lost, identically for both surfaces. The usage parser and the Sessions panel decode the same file on their own schedules -- after a restart the persistent store re-reads only changed files, so the panel may be the only surface that ever sees an unchanged broken one. Each calls this, with one wording per problem, so the registry above names a file once no matter which surface read it, and neither can be the silent one. The\n # cross-file copy dedup in _parse_all mints no new key, so this stays 1.\n persistent_parser_version = 1\n\n # Reasonix writes up to 9 fractional-second digits. datetime.fromisoformat\n # accepts only 3 or 6 before Python 3.11, and Tokdash supports 3.10, where\n # every row would otherwise be dropped as unparseable.\n _ISO_SUBSECOND_OVERFLOW = re.compile(r\"(\\.\\d{6})\\d+\")\n\n def __init__(self, pricing_db: PricingDatabase):\n super().__init__(pricing_db)\n self.stats_dir = clientpaths.reasonix_stats_dir()\n\n def _file_signatures(self) -> tuple:\n def scan() -> tuple:\n if not self.stats_dir.exists():\n return ()\n sigs: List[Tuple[str, int, int]] = []\n for p in self.stats_dir.glob(\"*.jsonl\"):\n try:\n s = p.stat()\n sigs.append((str(p), s.st_mtime_ns, s.st_size))\n except (FileNotFoundError, OSError):\n continue\n return tuple(sorted(sigs))\n\n return _timed_sigs(f\"reasonix:{self.stats_dir}\", scan)\n\n @staticmethod\n def _split_model(raw_model: str) -> Tuple[str, str]:\n raw = (raw_model or \"\").strip()\n if \"/\" in raw:\n parts = raw.split(\"/\", 1)\n return parts[0].strip(), parts[1].strip()\n return \"\", raw\n\n @staticmethod\n def _token_int(value: Any) -> Optional[int]:\n \"\"\"An explicit non-negative token count, or None when invalid.\n\n Mirrors dsh_log._to_int: a missing field is the caller's business, an\n unusable one rejects its row rather than raising into the per-file\n handler and silently discarding the rest of the day.\n \"\"\"\n if value is None:\n return None\n if isinstance(value, bool):\n return None\n try:\n result = int(value)\n except (TypeError, ValueError):\n return None\n return result if result >= 0 else None\n\n @classmethod\n def _token_field(cls, entry: Dict[str, Any], key: str) -> Optional[int]:\n \"\"\"A row's token count: 0 when absent, None when present but unusable.\n\n Absent is not malformed. until the vendor's write-slice semantics are verified.\n # 2: include usage-bearing function calls and other row types (#246).\n persistent_parser_version = 2\n\n def __init__(self, pricing_db: PricingDatabase):\n super().__init__(pricing_db)\n self.roots = clientpaths.workbuddy_roots()\n\n @staticmethod\n def _f(value: Any) -> float:\n try:\n return float(value)\n except (TypeError, ValueError):\n return 0.0\n\n @classmethod\n def _first_positive(cls, *values: Any) -> int:\n \"\"\"First value in the chain that is a positive integer, else 0.\"\"\"\n for value in values:\n n = cls._i(value)\n if n > 0:\n return n\n return 0\n\n def _usage_from_provider_data(self, pd: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:\n \"\"\"Normalize providerData.rawUsage (primary) or providerData.usage (fallback).\n\n Returns None when neither carries usable (non-zero) usage.\n \"\"\"\n ru = pd.get(\"rawUsage\")\n if isinstance(ru, dict) and ru:\n prompt = max(0, self._i(ru.get(\"prompt_tokens\")))\n details = ru.get(\"prompt_tokens_details\")\n # Comparing both scopes by stream position\n # lets a session/setModel admitted during a run take effect at the\n # next model-call boundary while preventing run n-1 state from\n # bleeding into run n.\n state_model: Optional[str] = None\n state_provider: Optional[str] = None\n run_id = payload.get(\"run_id\")\n best: Optional[Tuple[tuple, Optional[str], Optional[str]]] = None\n for pos, rec_model, rec_provider, rec_run, scope in state:\n if scope == \"run\" and (rec_run is None or rec_run != run_id):\n continue\n if scope not in (\"run\", \"session\"):\n continue\n if rec_model is None and rec_provider is None:\n continue\n if pos >= own_pos:\n continue\n if best is None or pos > best[0]:\n best = (pos, rec_model, rec_provider)\n if best is not None:\n _pos, state_model, state_provider = best\n # Field-wise per-call overrides (never pair-wise): the model on a\n # usage event is an observation, not a selection.\n model = percall_model if percall_model is not None else state_model\n provider = percall_provider if percall_provider is not None else state_provider\n return (model if model is not None else \"unknown\",\n provider if provider is not None else \"\")\n\n @staticmethod\n def _split_provider(model: str) -> Tuple[str, str]:\n \"\"\"Split a qualified provider/model id into BOTH fields. Splitting\n only the provider and keeping the qualified string in `model` is a\n stored-aggregation bug: aggregate_entries composes display names as\n f\\\"{provider}/{model}\\\", so a qualified model kept verbatim next to the\n extracted prefix surfaces as meta/meta/model, grouped apart from the\n same model's unqualified rows. Split once; a second \\\"/\\\" stays in.\"\"\"\n if \"/\" in model:\n provider, _, rest = model.partition(\"/\")\n if provider.strip() and rest.strip():\n return provider.strip(), rest.strip()\n return \"\", model\n\n def _parse_file_strict(self, file_sig: Tuple[str, int, int]) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:\n \"\"\"Strict single-file entry point for the stored sync.\n\n Raises UsageFileVanished (never returns []) when the enumerated file\n disappeared between discovery and open — under file_replace, [] means\n \\\"this file now has zero entries\\\" and the commit would delete every\n stored row for the path. sync_files catches the typed signal, verifies\n the path, and skips the file with its rows kept.\n \"\"\"\n records = self._read_records(file_sig)\n return self._build_entries(records, file_sig)\n\n def _parse_all(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:\n # The store's stable-key upsert keeps the earliest (timestamp,\n # file_path) copy of a record id that a fork restamped into a second\n # file; do the same here so live and persistent totals agree even when\n # a fork copies history — the same comparison the store's upsert\n # applies, tie included: fork copies stamped less than a millisecond\n # apart tie on timestamp_ms (entry timestamps are milliseconds) and\n # the lexicographically smallest path must win in BOTH modes.\n # The DB-off path is also the only place dedup can run at all:\n # cross_file_stable_keys lives inside sync_files, which\n # TOKDASH_USAGE_DB=0 bypasses.\n by_id: Dict[str, Tuple[tuple, Dict[str, Any]]] = {}\n for file_sig in self._file_signatures():\n try:\n entries = self._parse_file_strict(file_sig)\n except UsageFileVanished:\n # The DB-off live path skips ONLY the vanished file: every\n # other file's entries must survive the race, and the source\n # must never land in source_errors over a deletion (the\n # tracker's per-source except would blank the whole source).\n continue\n path = str(file_sig[0])\n for entry in entries:\n entry_id = entry[\"entry_id\"]\n key = (int(entry[\"timestamp\"]), path)\n prev = by_id.get(entry_id)\n if prev is None or key < prev[0]:\n by_id[entry_id] = (key, entry)\n entries = [entry for _key, entry in by_id.values()]\n entries.sort(key=lambda e: int(e.get(\"timestamp\", 0) or 0))\n return entries\n\n\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n# Crush (per-project crush.db)\n# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------\n\n\ndef _crush_ts_to_ms(value: Any) -> Optional[int]:\n \"\"\"Crush stamps ``strftime('%s','now')`` — seconds (the schema's\n \"milliseconds\" comment is stale). Scale guard: a value below 1e12\n is seconds (x1000); otherwise it is already ms.\"\"\"\n try:\n v = int(value)\n except (TypeError, ValueError):\n return None\n if v <= 0:\n return None\n if v < 1_000_000_000_000:\n return v * 1000\n return v\n\n\nclass CrushParser(BaseParser):\n \"\"\"\n Parser for Charm Crush (crush) session usage.\n\n =======================================================================\n CRUSH — PER-PROJECT crush.db, SESSION AGGREGATES\n =======================================================================\n Storage: clientpaths.crush_data_dirs() — $CRUSH_DATA_DIR, a\n comma-separated list of data dirs, each containing crush.db. Crush\n writes crush.db inside each project's data dir (default: .crush\n relative to the working directory) — there is no global root to\n scan, so Tokdash reads only the listed dirs.\n\n Read path: the DB is WAL-mode (connect.go sets journal_mode WAL),\n and a bare read-only connect to a live WAL DB is not enough (rows\n sit in the WAL), so each DB is read through the shared WAL snapshot\n helper (zcode_snapshot — first used by ZCodeParser: db + -wal are\n copied to a temp dir and re-opened).\n\n Shape: messages carry model/provider but no tokens, so the session\n counters are the only usage in the DB. NOT top-level only:\n Crush's own stats queries filter on parent_session_id IS NULL\n because they count sessions, and cost is the only thing Crush ever\n folds into a parent — coordinator.updateParentSessionCost is\n `parentSession.Cost += childSession.Cost` and touches no token\n field (verified in v0.91.2, the build behind the fixtures) — so a\n top-level-only filter drops every sub-agent's tokens outright. Each\n entry is attributed to its own session's last assistant message\n (role='assistant' AND is_summary_message=0, latest by created_at);\n mixed-model sessions price at the last model. sessions.cost is\n ignored — pricing DB only.\n\n The counters are a LAST-STEP snapshot, not a running total.\n sessions.sql has TWO writers with opposite semantics, and the\n accumulating one is not the agent's: UpdateSessionTitleAndUsage\n (`prompt_tokens = prompt_tokens + ?`) is used only by GenerateTitle,\n while the run loop assigns — agent.updateSessionTokenCounters is\n `session.CompletionTokens = usage.OutputTokens` /\n `session.PromptTokens = usage.InputTokens + usage.CacheReadTokens`\n with no `+=` — and saves through UpdateSession (`prompt_tokens = ?`,\n absolute), so every step overwrites the one before. The usage it\n assigns is one step's: OnStepFinish passes fallbackStepUsage(...,\n stepResult), which returns stepResult.Usage, and fantasy builds its\n TotalUsage by SUMMING that field across steps — a field the SDK\n accumulates cannot itself be cumulative. Note session.Cost += cost\n sits directly above the token assignment: cost accumulates, tokens\n do not, which is also why only cost folds into a parent.\n\n So the DB holds the final request's context size and the final\n turn's output; earlier steps are lost, and a Summarize run\n overwrites both with the summarizer's usage. The live capture is\n consistent with this but cannot prove it alone (15343/167 over 3\n steps fits either reading) — open item: a multi-turn run with\n provider-side totals before treating Crush numbers as billing-grade.\n\n Caveats (documented in SUPPORTED_CLIENTS.md): the last-step\n undercount above; tokens can be character-count estimates when the\n provider reports zero (no DB flag); the cache/reasoning split is not\n persisted (zero by construction); a session's total lands on its\n updated_at day (\"last touched\", not \"last used\").\n =======================================================================\n \"\"\"\n\n source_name = \"crush\"\n sync_capability = SourceSyncCapability(\n mode=\"file_replace\",\n cross_file_stable_keys=True,\n reason=(\n \"One WAL-mode crush.db per data dir; a session row is a mutable \"\n \"snapshot that Crush rewrites in place, so each sync replaces the \"\n \"source's rows with the current values.\"\n ),\n )\n # 1: one entry per session with non-zero tokens (sub-agents included),\n # model from the last assistant message, seconds timestamps,\n # pricing-DB cost only (sessions.cost ignored).\n # 2: copied sessions across project databases bill once, owned by the\n # earliest (timestamp, file_path), matching the usage store.\n persistent_parser_version = 2\n\n def __init__(self, pricing_db: PricingDatabase):\n super().__init__(pricing_db)\n self.data_dirs = clientpaths.crush_data_dirs()\n\n def _db_paths(self) -> List[Path]:\n return [d / \"crush.db\" for d in self.data_dirs]\n\n def _file_signatures(self) -> tuple:\n def scan() -> tuple:\n out: List[Tuple[str, int, int]] = []\n for db in self._db_paths():\n # ONE entry per project DB, WAL sidecars folded in\n # (_sqlite_db_signature). A per-sidecar entry would make\n # file_replace sync snapshot and reparse each DB two or\n # three times per sync.\n sig = _sqlite_db_signature(db)\n if sig is not None:\n out.append(sig)\n return tuple(out)\n\n return _timed_sigs(\n \"crush:\" + \",\".join(str(d) for d in self.data_dirs), scan\n )\n\n def _parse_db(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:\n conn.row_factory = sqlite3.Row\n # is_summary_message was added by migration 20250810000000 and is\n # not in initial.sql, but Crush runs goose.Up on every open\n # (connect.go), so any DB a post-2025-08-10 build has opened\n # already has the column backfilled. The PRAGMA check is cheap\n # insurance for a pre-migration file only.\n cols = {str(r[1]) for r in conn.execute(\"PRAGMA table_info(messages)\").fetchall()}\n summary_filter = \" AND is_summary_message = 0\" if \"is_summary_message\" in cols else \"\"\n last_model: Dict[str, Tuple[Optional[str], Optional[str]]] = {}\n for row in conn.execute(\n \"SELECT session_id, model, provider, created_at FROM messages \"\n f\"WHERE role = 'assistant'{summary_filter} \"\n \"ORDER BY session_id, created_at DESC\"\n ):\n sid = str(row[\"session_id\"] or \"\")\n if sid and sid not in last_model:\n last_model[sid] = (row[\"model\"], row[\"provider\"])\n out: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []\n for row in conn.execute(\n \"SELECT id, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens, updated_at FROM sessions \"\n \"WHERE (prompt_tokens + completion_tokens) > 0\"\n ):\n sid = str(row[\"id\"] or \"\")\n if not sid:\n continue\n ts_ms = _crush_ts_to_ms(row[\"updated_at\"])\n if ts_ms is None:\n continue\n model, provider = last_model.get(sid, (None, None))\n model = str(model).strip() if model is not None else \"\"\n provider = str(provider).strip() if provider is not None else \"\"\n if not model:\n model, provider = \"unknown\", \"unknown\"\n input_t = self._i(row[\"prompt_tokens\"])\n output_t = self._i(row[\"completion_tokens\"])\n out.append({\n \"source\": self.source_name,\n \"model\": model,\n \"provider\": provider,\n \"input\": input_t,\n \"output\": output_t,\n \"cacheRead\": 0,\n \"cacheWrite\": 0,\n \"reasoning\": 0,\n \"cost\": self.pricing_db.get_cost(model, input_t, output_t, 0, 0),\n \"timestamp\": ts_ms,\n \"entry_id\": f\"crush:{sid}\",\n \"_billing\": usage_billing_pricing(\n [model],\n input_tokens=input_t,\n output_tokens=output_t,\n cache_read=0,\n cache_write=0,\n ),\n })\n return out\n\n def _parse_all(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:\n winners: Dict[str, Tuple[Tuple[int, str], Dict[str, Any]]] = {}\n # Driven off _file_signatures() so file_replace sync's injected\n # single-file scope reparses one project DB, not all of them.\n for path_str, _, _ in self._file_signatures():\n db = Path(path_str)\n try:\n # Shared WAL-snapshot helper (first user: ZCodeParser);\n # see its docstring for the coherence semantics.\n with zcode_snapshot(db) as snap:\n for entry in self._parse_db(snap.conn):\n position = (entry[\"timestamp\"], path_str)\n previous = winners.get(entry[\"entry_id\"])\n if previous is None or position < previous[0]:\n winners[entry[\"entry_id\"]] = (position, entry)\n except (ZCodeSnapshotError, sqlite3.Error, OSError):\n # A locked or corrupt per-project DB must not blank the\n # others; the signatures move with Crush's next write, so\n # the next collect retries.\n logger.warning(\"crush db %s unreadable; skipped\", db, exc_info=True)\n continue\n return [entry for _position, entry in winners.values()]\n\n\nclass MiniMaxCodeParser(BaseParser):\n \"\"\"\n Parser for MiniMax Code (npm ``@minimax-ai/code``, CLI ``mcode``).\n\n =======================================================================\n MINIMAX CODE — DATED SESSION DIRS, ONE ENTRY PER ASSISTANT CALL\n =======================================================================\n Storage (verified against an installed v0.4.12): the harness home is\n ``$MINIMAX_DATA_DIR``, else the legacy ``$MAVIS_DATA_DIR``, else\n ``~/.minimax``; each session is one directory under\n ``/v2/sessions/YYYY/MM/DD/-session_/`` (nested date\n shard; the session ``manifest.json`` records ``layout:\n \"v2-final-dated-session\"``) holding the append-only transcript\n ``messages.jsonl``. The directory also\n carries a\n ``manifest.json``, request captures (``llm-call.json``) and a\n ``history-catalog.json``; none adds usage the transcript does not already\n carry, and the SQLite projection beside them\n (``v2/sqlite/runtime-state.sqlite``, table\n ``local_runtime_token_usage``) folds one row per TURN — losing per-call\n resolution while the transcript keeps every call — so the transcript is\n the source and the DB is not read.\n\n Rows: one JSON object per message, ``{message_id, turn_id, message}``.\n Only ``message.role == \"assistant\"`` rows are billable; each carries the\n call's ``model`` / ``provider`` and a\n ``usage{input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, totalTokens,\n cost{input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, total}}`` object.\n The four token fields are already disjoint: the capture verifies\n ``totalTokens == input + output + cacheRead + cacheWrite``, so they map\n onto the four buckets verbatim with no subtraction — unlike the\n cache-inclusive prompts of Qwen/WorkBuddy. That identity is the whole\n basis for verbatim pass-through, so the parser re-checks it per row and\n warns once per pass when it breaks: a future cache-inclusive build then\n surfaces as a log signal instead of a silent cacheRead double-count.\n ``cost`` is the harness's own billing estimate — a per-bucket object\n with a ``total``, all-zero in the capture (MiniMax's subscription plan\n reports no per-call USD); Tokdash never reads it and prices from the\n pricing DB instead, so a real per-call cost there would price a row the\n harness left at 0.\n ``message.timestamp`` is epoch milliseconds — verified against the\n transcript, the ``llm-call.json`` captures and the SQLite projection on\n the live install — so the ``timestamp > 0`` sanity check needs no unit\n guard (same bar as Cline/Qwen).\n\n ``message_id`` (``msg-``) is the dedup key. It is unique within\n a transcript (a duplicate is a rewrite, dropped) and, because ids are\n minted per message, a fork that copies the parent's rows verbatim would\n carry the same ids — cross_file_stable_keys lets the usage store own\n those keys by earliest occurrence (Codex/Cline precedent). Whether\n MiniMax's history-fork flow copies or remints ids is capture-pending; a\n reminting fork would read as new calls, the same standing caveat Muse\n documents for its forks.\n\n A model switch mid-session needs no state walk: every row carries its own\n ``model``, so each call prices at the model that made it (per-row, like\n Codex; nothing to carry over, unlike Muse's selection records).\n =======================================================================\n \"\"\"\n\n source_name = \"minimax\"\n sync_capability = SourceSyncCapability(\n mode=\"file_replace\",\n append_jsonl=True,\n cross_file_stable_keys=True,\n reason=(\n \"messages.jsonl is append-only and every assistant row is \"\n \"self-contained (own model, own usage), so an appended tail is \"\n \"complete on its own; message_id is stable across copied forks.\"\n ),\n )\n # 1: disjoint buckets from the usage object verbatim, priced from the\n # pricing DB; message_id keys.\n persistent_parser_version = 1\n # Re-armed by _parse_all each pass; guards the one-warning drift signal.\n _drift_warned = False\n\n def _file_signatures(self) -> tuple:\n items: List[Tuple[str, int, int]] = []\n for path in clientpaths.minimax_code_session_files():\n try:\n stat = path.stat()\n except OSError:\n continue\n items.append((str(path), int(stat.st_mtime_ns), int(stat.st_size)))\n return tuple(items)\n\n def _entry_from_row(self, record: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:\n msg = record.get(\"message\")\n if not isinstance(msg, dict) or msg.get(\"role\") != \"assistant\":\n return None\n usage = msg.get(\"usage\")\n if not isinstance(usage, dict):\n return None\n input_t = max(0, self._i(usage.get(\"input\")))\n output_t = max(0, self._i(usage.get(\"output\")))\n cache_r = max(0, self._i(usage.get(\"cacheRead\")))\n cache_w = max(0, self._i(usage.get(\"cacheWrite\")))\n bucket_sum = input_t + output_t + cache_r + cache_w\n if bucket_sum <= 0:\n return None\n ts_ms = self._i(msg.get(\"timestamp\"))\n if ts_ms <= 0:\n return None\n msg_id = record.get(\"message_id\")\n if msg_id:\n msg_id = str(msg_id)\n\n model = str(msg.get(\"model\") or \"unknown\")\n provider = str(msg.get(\"provider\") or \"\")\n\n # Verbatim pass-through is only sound while the buckets stay\n # disjoint. If a future build goes cache-inclusive (Qwen/WorkBuddy\n # style), the declared total stops matching the sum — warn once per\n # pass so the drift is visible instead of silently double-counting\n # cacheRead.\n total_t = self._i(usage.get(\"totalTokens\"))\n if total_t > 0 and total_t != bucket_sum and not self._drift_warned:\n self._drift_warned = True\n logger.warning(\n \"minimax: usage buckets no longer disjoint in %s: \"\n \"totalTokens=%s != input+output+cacheRead+cacheWrite=%s\",\n model, total_t, bucket_sum,\n )\n\n return {\n \"source\": self.source_name,\n \"model\": model,\n \"provider\": provider,\n \"input\": input_t,\n \"output\": output_t,\n \"cacheRead\": cache_r,\n \"cacheWrite\": cache_w,\n \"reasoning\": 0,\n \"cost\": self.pricing_db.get_cost(model, input_t, output_t, cache_r, cache_w),\n \"timestamp\": int(ts_ms),\n \"entry_id\": f\"minimax:{msg_id}\" if msg_id else \"\",\n \"_billing\": usage_billing_pricing(\n [model],\n input_tokens=input_t,\n output_tokens=output_t,\n cache_read=cache_r,\n cache_write=cache_w,\n ),\n }\n\n def _parse_all(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:\n # The store's stable-key upsert keeps the earliest-timestamped\n # occurrence of a copied id; do the same here so live and\n # persistent totals agree even when a fork restamps a copy (Cline/\n # Qwen precedent). Within one transcript a repeated message_id is a\n # rewrite, not a new call; ties keep the first-seen occurrence, and\n # files scan in sorted-path order, matching the store's\n # earliest-(timestamp, path) ownership.\n by_id: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}\n anonymous: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []\n self._drift_warned = False\n for path_str, _, _ in self._file_signatures():\n try:\n handle = open(path_str, \"r\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n except OSError:\n continue\n with handle:\n for line in handle:\n line = line.strip()\n if not line:\n continue\n try:\n record = json.loads(line)\n entry = (\n self._entry_from_row(record)\n if isinstance(record, dict)\n else None\n )\n except Exception:\n logger.warning(\"minimax: skipping malformed row in %s\", path_str)\n entry = None\n if entry is None:\n continue\n entry_id = entry[\"entry_id\"]\n if not entry_id:\n anonymous.append(entry)\n continue\n prev = by_id.get(entry_id)\n if prev is None or entry[\"timestamp\"] < prev[\"timestamp\"]:\n by_id[entry_id] = entry\n out = list(by_id.values()) + anonymous\n out.sort(key=lambda item: int(item.get(\"timestamp\", 0) or 0))\n return out\n\n\nclass DevinParser(BaseParser):\n \"\"\"\n Parser for Devin CLI (Cognition) token usage.\n\n =======================================================================\n DEVIN CLI -- CLOSED-SOURCE RUST CLI, ONE SQLITE STORE, NO CLI LOG PARSE\n =======================================================================\n Verified from Devin CLI 3000.10.31 (the schema and record fields compiled\n into the binary, plus its shipped docs bundle; recorded in\n docs/local/20260921_devin_cli_support/evidence/):\n\n * Store: ``sessions.db`` in the CLI data dir, WAL mode with -wal/-shm.\n Linux and macOS use ``~/.local/share/devin/cli``, Windows uses\n ``%APPDATA%\\\\devin\\\\cli`` -- all three from the vendor's own\n troubleshooting page, quoted in evidence/03. clientpaths.devin_db_paths()\n resolves them, including the Windows-host store seen from WSL, and also\n tries ``~/Library/Application Support/devin/cli`` on macOS in case the\n Rust build maps app data there instead.\n * ``message_nodes`` is the conversation forest, one row per node, the whole\n message as JSON in ``chat_message``. A migration DROPs the older flat\n ``messages`` table, so there is no legacy table to read.\n * The per-call record carries explicit ``input_tokens``,\n ``output_tokens``, ``cache_read_tokens`` and ``cache_creation_tokens``.\n Tokens are read, never inferred.\n * ``sessions.model`` is the session's model and ``sessions.hidden`` marks\n internal helper sessions (the summarizer).\n\n NOT yet confirmed against a populated store -- no Devin install exists on the\n dev machines and the CLI cannot be pointed at a local model, so a trial\n capture is required (Q1-Q12 in FINDINGS.md). The behaviour chosen for each\n gap, and why:\n\n * cache convention (Q3): treated as cache-EXCLUSIVE, input + cacheRead =\n the full prompt. These are the Anthropic usage names, where cache reads\n are a separate bucket from input. If the capture shows the opposite, the\n split flips and ``test_cache_split_is_exclusive_and_documented`` is\n the test that says so.\n * model attribution (Q4): the node's own model when the record carries\n one, else the session model. A Fusion/Adaptive session billed on a model\n other than the selected one can therefore be priced at the selected\n model, which is the documented limit until the capture shows the field.\n * cost (Q2): pricing-DB only. Devin publishes no per-token rate card and\n is sold as seats plus credits, so Cognition-hosted models (``swe-*``,\n Fusion pairings) resolve to 0.00. The client does receive a vendor USD\n estimate from the server; nothing of it is known to be persisted, and a\n streamed number is not a local file, so none is read.\n * reasoning: no bucket exists upstream, so it is 0 by construction rather\n than an estimate.\n * timestamp unit (Q7): not pinned by the capture either, so the reader is\n tolerant rather than binary. Seconds, milliseconds, microseconds and\n nanoseconds are each normalized to ms by magnitude. A seconds-or-ms test\n alone would read a ``as_micros()`` store as milliseconds, put every row a\n thousand years out, and report zero usage for the all-time window with\n nothing in the log -- the worst possible failure this source can have.\n * hidden helper sessions COUNT. A summarizer call spends real quota, and\n it lives in its own session row, so it is not a copy of a counted parent\n call. Q9 re-checks that.\n\n Reads never write. _needs_snapshot() decides per store: a drvfs mount, a UNC\n path or a live -wal/-shm sidecar means copy-first, because a WAL database can\n need recovery or -shm creation, which a mode=ro open cannot do and which\n connect_sqlite_readonly's read-write fallback WOULD do inside the user's\n store. A local store with no sidecars is opened read-only, and if even that\n fails the read is retried once through a copy before it is reported. A store\n that cannot be read at all is logged and left out of the result without being\n cached, so a transient failure never settles into a cached zero.\n\n Reach is one-directional: a Tokdash running in WSL sees the Windows host\n store, but a Tokdash running on Windows does not see a guest store behind\n \\\\\\\\wsl.localhost\\\\\\\\... (see the note on clientpaths.devin_cli_roots).\n DEVIN_CLI_DATA_DIRS with the UNC path is the escape hatch.\n =======================================================================\n \"\"\"\n\n source_name = \"devin\"\n sync_capability = SourceSyncCapability(\n mode=\"source_native_db\",\n session_store=False,\n reason=\"Devin CLI keeps its history in one SQLite DB and supports SQL date windows.\",\n )\n # Queried live; rows are never copied into usage_entries, so nothing is stored\n # for a version to identify.\n persistent_parser_version = None\n\n # Per-query cache, same shape as OpenCodeParser: {(s_ms, u_ms): entries}.\n # Redeclared here rather than inherited -- a subclass that inherits the base\n # dict while assigning its own signature serves one source's rows to another.\n _query_cache: ClassVar[Dict[tuple, List[Dict[str, Any]]]] = {}\n _query_cache_sig: ClassVar[tuple] = ()\n _QUERY_CACHE_MAX: ClassVar[int] = 32\n\n # Timestamp unit floors. Each one sits below every real epoch value in its\n # own unit and above every plausible value in the next-coarser unit, so the\n # tier a value lands in is decided by magnitude alone.\n #\n # The ns and us floors are 1e8 seconds written in that unit (1973-03-03).\n # The ms floor is NOT: 1e12 ms is 1e9 seconds, i.e. 2001-09-09, a decade\n # higher on purpose. Nothing writes an ms timestamp from before 2001, and\n # putting the s/ms boundary at 1e12 rather than 1e11 leaves the seconds\n # tier correct to the year 33658 instead of 5138. Upper ends: an ms store\n # reads as ms until 1e14 ms and a us store as us until 1e17 us, both the\n # year 5138.\n #\n # Three floors and a seconds fallthrough, not one floor, because a two-way\n # test is silently catastrophic.\n # A Rust CLI reaching for as_micros() or as_nanos() writes 1.7e15 or 1.7e18;\n # a seconds-or-ms test reads that as milliseconds, lands it a thousand years\n # in the future, and drops every row against the window ceiling -- zero\n # usage, no failure, no log, even for the all-time window. A tolerant reader\n # costs one comparison and cannot be wrong about a store that is already\n # readable; the capture pins which unit this store actually uses (Q7), but\n # nothing about the capture can make a µs store impossible tomorrow.\n _TS_NS_FLOOR: ClassVar[int] = 100_000_000_000_000_000 # 1e17 ns = 1973\n _TS_US_FLOOR: ClassVar[int] = 100_000_000_000_000 # 1e14 us = 1973\n _TS_MS_FLOOR: ClassVar[int] = 1_000_000_000_000 # 1e12 ms = 2001\n\n _TOKEN_FIELDS: ClassVar[Tuple[str, ...]] = (\n \"input_tokens\",\n \"output_tokens\",\n \"cache_read_tokens\",\n \"cache_creation_tokens\",\n )\n # Where a usage object may sit inside a node's JSON, in precedence order,\n # dotted for a nested one. Explicit locations only, each bounded to the\n # depth written here: a recursive hunt would find the usage echoed in tool\n # output (``message.tool_result``) and bill it, which is why the list names\n # every parent it will enter and ``tool_result`` is not among them.\n #\n # The root and the four single-word guesses are cheap insurance. The rest\n # are not guesses: evidence/03 section 4 records the node JSON's own keys as\n # ``id``, ``message``, ``parent_id``, ``summarized_from``,\n # ``num_tokens_preceding`` and ``extensions``, and names the per-call struct\n # ``PerformanceMetrics``. So ``message`` and ``extensions`` are the two\n # documented places a nested container can sit, and\n # ``performance_metrics``/``performanceMetrics`` are what serde writes for\n # that struct under either rename convention. A miss costs one dict lookup;\n # the wrong list costs every token this source would ever report, and only\n # the tripwire in collect() would say so (Q3/Q4 settle it).\n #\n # The ``metadata.*`` paths come from a populated store rather than the\n # binary docs: a real ``chat_message`` payload carries ``metadata.metrics``\n # holding ``input_tokens``/``output_tokens``/``cache_read_tokens``/\n # ``cache_creation_tokens`` beside ``ttft_ms`` and friends.\n _USAGE_PATHS: ClassVar[Tuple[str, ...]] = (\n \"\",\n \"usage\",\n \"metrics\",\n \"performance\",\n \"performance_metrics\",\n \"performanceMetrics\",\n \"telemetry\",\n \"message.usage\",\n \"message.performance_metrics\",\n \"message.performanceMetrics\",\n \"message\",\n \"metadata.metrics\",\n \"metadata.usage\",\n \"metadata.performance_metrics\",\n \"metadata.performanceMetrics\",\n \"extensions.usage\",\n \"extensions.performance_metrics\",\n \"extensions.performanceMetrics\",\n \"extensions\",\n )\n _MODEL_FIELDS: ClassVar[Tuple[str, ...]] = (\n \"model\",\n \"modelId\",\n \"model_id\",\n \"modelUid\",\n \"model_uid\",\n \"generation_model\",\n \"generationModel\",\n )\n @classmethod\n def _ts_ms_sql(cls, column: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"`column` normalized to milliseconds, as a SQL expression.\n\n SQLite's `/` between two integers is integer division, which is what the\n ns and us tiers want. The floors are literals rather than bound\n parameters on purpose: the expression appears twice per query, because\n WHERE cannot see a SELECT alias, so placeholders would put eight values\n in one tuple whose order is the entire risk and is invisible in the\n query text.\n \"\"\"\n return (\n f\"CASE WHEN {column} >= {cls._TS_NS_FLOOR} THEN {column} / 1000000 \"\n f\"WHEN {column} >= {cls._TS_US_FLOOR} THEN {column} / 1000 \"\n f\"WHEN {column} >= {cls._TS_MS_FLOOR} THEN {column} \"\n f\"ELSE {column} * 1000 END\"\n )\n\n def __init__(self, pricing_db: PricingDatabase):\n super().__init__(pricing_db)\n self.db_paths = clientpaths.devin_db_paths()\n\n # -- reading ---------------------------------------------------------------\n\n def _file_signatures(self) -> tuple:\n # db + -wal + -shm, the ZCodeParser._file_signatures set. The -shm looks\n # removable because the snapshot path excludes it, but that helper\n # signatures what it COPIES; this one is the invalidation clock, and a\n # WAL store's live rows move through -wal and -shm between checkpoints.\n # Dropping either sidecar would serve stale usage while the CLI runs.\n # Extra busts from reader traffic re-run a bounded query; missed busts\n # are silent lag, which is the failure this source cannot afford.\n out: List[Tuple[str, Optional[int], Optional[int]]] = []\n for db in self.db_paths:\n for candidate in (db, Path(str(db) + \"-wal\"), Path(str(db) + \"-shm\")):\n try:\n st = candidate.stat()\n out.append((str(candidate), st.st_mtime_ns, st.st_size))\n except (FileNotFoundError, OSError):\n out.append((str(candidate), None, None))\n return tuple(out)\n\n @staticmethod\n def _needs_snapshot(db_path: Path) -> bool:\n \"\"\"True when opening this store in place is unsafe or impossible.\n\n Three cases, decided on transport and on-disk state rather than on\n where the path came from:\n\n * a Windows drive seen through WSL's drvfs mount (``/mnt//``);\n * a UNC path (``\\\\\\\\wsl.localhost\\\\\\\\...``, ``\\\\\\\\wsl$\\\\...``, or any\n other share). This is how a Windows-host Tokdash reaches a guest store, see\n ``clientpaths.devin_cli_roots``; pathlib's parsing of both this and the\n drvfs shape is platform-dependent, so both are decided on the path text;\n * any store with a live ``-wal`` or ``-shm`` sidecar.\n\n The reason is the same in all three, and it is not only about read\n integrity. A WAL database that needs recovery, or that has to create\n its ``-shm``, cannot be opened ``mode=ro`` -- and\n ``connect_sqlite_readonly`` answers that failure with a read-WRITE\n connect. Tokdash would then run WAL recovery inside the user's store\n and create sidecar files next to it. Over 9p the locking is unreliable\n on top of that. Copying first is both safe and side-effect-free, which\n is what ZCode already does for the same hazard.\n \"\"\"\n # Both tests read the path as text, never through the host's path\n # flavour. A WindowsPath splits \"/mnt/c/...\" with a \"\\\\\" root and a UNC\n # path into a \"\\\\\\\\server\\\\share\\\\\" drive, so a parts-based test answers\n # by which OS is asking rather than by which store it was handed --\n # and these two shapes exist precisely because a store is reached from\n # the other side of a mount.\n text = str(db_path).replace(\"\\\\\", \"/\")\n if text.startswith(\"//\"):\n return True\n parts = text.split(\"/\")\n if len(parts) > 2 and parts[0] == \"\" and parts[1] == \"mnt\" and len(parts[2]) == 1:\n return True\n for suffix in (\"-wal\", \"-shm\"):\n try:\n if Path(str(db_path) + suffix).exists():\n return True\n except OSError:\n # Cannot rule the sidecar out, so cannot rule recovery out.\n return True\n return False\n\n def _read_via_snapshot(\n self, db_path: Path, s_ms: int, u_ms: int\n ) -> Tuple[List[tuple], Optional[str]]:\n \"\"\"Copy the store to a temp dir and read the copy. Never writes to the source.\"\"\"\n snap = None\n try:\n with zcode_snapshot(db_path) as snap:\n try:\n rows = self._rows(snap.conn, s_ms, u_ms)\n except sqlite3.Error as exc:\n return [], f\"query failed: {exc}\"\n except ZCodeSnapshotError as exc:\n return [], f\"snapshot failed: {exc}\"\n # close_failed is only set once the snapshot has exited, so the check\n # belongs after the with block. The rows are fine, but a snapshot that\n # could not be closed is a failed read by ZCode's rule, reported so the\n # caller skips the cache write.\n if snap is not None and snap.close_failed:\n return rows, \"snapshot close failed\"\n return rows, None\n\n def _read_store(\n self, db_path: Path, s_ms: int, u_ms: int\n ) -> Tuple[List[tuple], Optional[str]]:\n \"\"\"Read one store. Returns ``(rows, error)``, with error None on a clean read.\n\n Failures are reported instead of swallowed. A store that could not be\n copied, connected or queried yields no rows, and the caller must not\n cache that: a hiccup usually leaves the file signatures alone, so a\n cached empty result would read as \"no Devin usage\" until the next Devin\n run busts the signature.\n \"\"\"\n if self._needs_snapshot(db_path):\n return self._read_via_snapshot(db_path, s_ms, u_ms)\n\n try:\n conn = connect_sqlite_readonly(db_path)\n except Exception as exc:\n # A connect can succeed on a file that is not a database at all; the\n # first statement in _rows is where that surfaces, as sqlite3.Error.\n return [], f\"connect failed: {exc}\"\n\n error: Optional[str] = None\n try:\n return self._rows(conn, s_ms, u_ms), None\n except sqlite3.OperationalError as exc:\n error = f\"query failed: {exc}\"\n except sqlite3.Error as exc:\n # DatabaseError and friends mean \"this is not a database\", which no\n # amount of copying fixes, so it is reported without a retry.\n return [], f\"query failed: {exc}\"\n finally:\n try:\n conn.close()\n except Exception:\n pass\n\n # OperationalError on a local store that looked fine is usually a WAL\n # database that needs recovery or an -shm it was not allowed to create.\n # Retrying through a copy is the safe direction, so try it before\n # reporting a failure that would otherwise repeat every poll until the\n # user happens to run Devin again.\n snap_rows, snap_error = self._read_via_snapshot(db_path, s_ms, u_ms)\n if snap_error is None:\n return snap_rows, None\n return [], f\"{error} (snapshot retry: {snap_error})\"\n\n def _rows(self, conn: sqlite3.Connection, s_ms: int, u_ms: int) -> List[tuple]:\n # sqlite3.Error propagates to _read_store, which turns it into a failed,\n # uncached read. An absent table is a legitimate empty store and is safe\n # to cache; a probe error is not, so the two must not be conflated here.\n tables = {\n row[0]\n for row in conn.execute(\n \"SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type='table'\"\n \" AND name IN ('message_nodes','sessions')\"\n )\n }\n if \"message_nodes\" not in tables:\n # Not a Devin store, or a version whose forest table is named\n # differently. Reading nothing is correct: a guess here invents usage.\n return []\n # Built once and reused for both the projection and the window: if the\n # two copies ever disagreed, rows would be filtered on one unit and\n # reported on another.\n ts_ms = self._ts_ms_sql(\"n.created_at\")\n params: tuple = (s_ms, u_ms)\n if \"sessions\" in tables:\n query = (\n \"SELECT n.session_id, n.node_id, n.chat_message, \"\n f\"{ts_ms} AS ts_ms, s.model \"\n \"FROM message_nodes n LEFT JOIN sessions s ON s.id = n.session_id \"\n f\"WHERE {ts_ms} >= ? AND {ts_ms} < ?\"\n )\n else:\n query = (\n \"SELECT n.session_id, n.node_id, n.chat_message, \"\n f\"{ts_ms} AS ts_ms, NULL \"\n \"FROM message_nodes n \"\n f\"WHERE {ts_ms} >= ? AND {ts_ms} < ?\"\n )\n # No try/except here: a schema this parser does not know, or a store that\n # is not SQLite at all, must reach _read_store as sqlite3.Error so the\n # caller can report it and skip the cache write. Swallowing it here would\n # let a schema-drifted store read as a verified-empty one.\n return list(conn.execute(query, params))\n\n # -- record extraction -----------------------------------------------------\n\n def _usage_container(self, node: Dict[str, Any]) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:\n for location in self._USAGE_PATHS:\n container: Any = node\n for key in location.split(\".\") if location else ():\n if not isinstance(container, dict):\n container = None\n break\n container = container.get(key)\n if not isinstance(container, dict):\n continue\n if any(field in container for field in self._TOKEN_FIELDS):\n return container\n return None\n\n def _model_of(self, node: Dict[str, Any], usage: Dict[str, Any]) -> str:\n # A populated store names the model at ``metadata.generation_model``\n # (``swe-2-high``, ``summarizer``, ...), so ``metadata`` is checked\n # alongside the node and the usage container.\n metadata = node.get(\"metadata\")\n containers = (node, usage, metadata) if isinstance(metadata, dict) else (node, usage)\n for container in containers:\n for field in self._MODEL_FIELDS:\n value = container.get(field)\n if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip():\n return value.strip()\n return \"\"\n\n def _build_entry(\n self,\n session_id: str,\n node_id: Any,\n node: Dict[str, Any],\n session_model: Any,\n ts_ms: int,\n ) -> Optional[Dict[str, Any]]:\n usage = self._usage_container(node)\n if usage is None:\n return None\n input_t = self._i(usage.get(\"input_tokens\"))\n output_t = self._i(usage.get(\"output_tokens\"))\n cache_r = self._i(usage.get(\"cache_read_tokens\"))\n cache_w = self._i(usage.get(\"cache_creation_tokens\"))\n if input_t + output_t + cache_r + cache_w <= 0:\n # A zero-usage record is not a billable call (a user row, a\n # cancelled request). Skipping it is what keeps a replay out of the\n # totals, and it is the same filter the other DB sources use.\n return None\n\n # Live stores name it ``message_id``; ``id`` covers the documented\n # shape and any other writer.\n message_id = node.get(\"id\") or node.get(\"message_id\")\n entry_id = (\n f\"devin:{session_id}:{message_id}\"\n if isinstance(message_id, str) and message_id.strip()\n else f\"devin:{session_id}:{node_id}\"\n )\n model = self._model_of(node, usage) or (str(session_model).strip() if session_model else \"\")\n model = model or \"unknown\"\n return {\n \"source\": self.source_name,\n \"model\": model,\n \"provider\": \"\",\n \"input\": input_t,\n \"output\": output_t,\n \"cacheRead\": cache_r,\n \"cacheWrite\": cache_w,\n # Devin persists no reasoning bucket, so this is zero by\n # construction, not an omitted measurement.\n \"reasoning\": 0,\n \"cost\": self.pricing_db.get_cost(model, input_t, output_t, cache_r, cache_w),\n \"timestamp\": int(ts_ms),\n \"entry_id\": entry_id,\n }\n\n # -- collect ---------------------------------------------------------------\n\n def _parse_all(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:\n return [] # collect() is overridden; this satisfies the ABC contract\n\n def collect(self, since_date: Optional[datetime] = None, until_date: Optional[datetime] = None) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:\n \"\"\"SQL-window read with per-query caching, as OpenCode and Kilo do.\n\n The store holds full transcripts, so the date filter stays in SQL rather\n than pulling every node into memory. Cached per (store signature, pricing\n signature, window) and bounded, so a large history is parsed once.\n \"\"\"\n sig = (\n self._file_signatures(),\n self._pricing_signature(),\n self.runtime_config_signature(),\n )\n if sig != type(self)._query_cache_sig:\n type(self)._query_cache.clear()\n type(self)._query_cache_sig = sig\n\n s_ms = int(self._to_utc(since_date).timestamp() * 1000) if since_date else 0\n u_ms = int(self._to_utc(until_date).timestamp() * 1000) if until_date else 9999999999999\n cache_key = (s_ms, u_ms)\n cached = type(self)._query_cache.get(cache_key)\n if cached is not None:\n return list(cached)\n\n rows: List[tuple] = []\n failures: List[str] = []\n for db_path in self.db_paths:\n store_rows, error = self._read_store(db_path, s_ms, u_ms)\n if error is not None:\n # Loud on the log, quiet on the dashboard: a store that could not\n # be read is not a store with zero usage in it.\n logger.warning(\"tokdash devin: %s read failed, not cached (%s)\", db_path, error)\n failures.append(error)\n rows.extend(store_rows)\n\n # Oldest first, so a duplicated record is owned by its earliest copy --\n # the same rule the usage store applies to forked transcripts.\n rows.sort(key=lambda row: int(row[3] or 0))\n out: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []\n seen: set = set()\n containerless = 0\n for session_id, node_id, chat_message, ts_ms, session_model in rows:\n try:\n node = json.loads(chat_message)\n except (TypeError, ValueError):\n containerless += 1\n continue\n if not isinstance(node, dict):\n containerless += 1\n continue\n entry = self._build_entry(\n str(session_id), node_id, node, session_model, int(ts_ms or 0)\n )\n if entry is None:\n # Two different nothings. A usage object that reported zero is a\n # user row or a cancelled request, which is normal; a row with no\n # usage object at any known location is the interesting one.\n if self._usage_container(node) is None:\n containerless += 1\n continue\n if entry[\"entry_id\"] in seen:\n continue\n seen.add(entry[\"entry_id\"])\n out.append(entry)\n\n if rows and containerless == len(rows):\n # Rows in the window, not one of them carrying a usage object. That\n # is what a relocated usage layout looks like, and without this line\n # it is indistinguishable from an idle week: the dashboard shows a\n # clean zero and every assumption in _USAGE_PATHS stays untested.\n logger.warning(\n \"tokdash devin: %d node(s) in the window and none carried a usage\"\n \" container; check _USAGE_PATHS against the current store\",\n len(rows),\n )\n\n # Partial or failed reads are returned but not cached: the signatures\n # that guard this cache may not have moved, so a cached zero would outlive\n # the hiccup. Same rule the ZCode collectors follow.\n if failures:\n return out\n\n if len(type(self)._query_cache) >= self._QUERY_CACHE_MAX:\n type(self)._query_cache.clear()\n type(self)._query_cache[cache_key] = out\n return list(out)\n\n\nclass FreebuffParser(BaseParser):\n \"\"\"\n Parser for Freebuff Desktop's per-project SQLite stores.\n\n =======================================================================\n FREEBUFF DESKTOP — ONE desktop-v2.db PER PROJECT, ONE ENTRY PER TURN\n =======================================================================\n Storage: ``~/.config/freebuff-desktop/projects/-/\n desktop-v2.db`` (see clientpaths.freebuff_desktop_db_paths). The desktop\n app is an Electron build whose renderer owns the UI while a separate\n ``orchestrator.js`` process (a Bun bundle) writes every thread and message\n into one SQLite store per opened project. The directory name carries the\n project basename plus a UUID; the authoritative project path is in the\n sibling ``project.json``.\n\n This is NOT the Freebuff CLI: the CLI (``.config/manicode``, npm\n ``freebuff``) writes per-chat ``chat-messages.json`` / ``run-state.json``\n trees under ``getConfigDir()/projects//chats//``, and\n those files carry no token counters at all (the ChatMessage type has a\n ``credits`` field and no usage object). Only the desktop store persists\n per-call usage, so only the desktop store is read.\n\n Schema (verified against the shipped orchestrator bundle and four live\n stores):\n threads(id, project_id, project_path, title, model, harness_id,\n agent_mode, created_at, ...) — one row per conversation.\n messages(seq INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT, thread_id, role,\n parts_json, metrics_json, ts, ...) — one row per message.\n\n Rows: TWO tables carry billable usage, and both are read.\n\n 1. ``messages.metrics_json`` → ``usage``, on ``role = 'assistant'`` rows.\n A live capture holds exactly one assistant row per user turn (verified:\n 29 user / 28 assistant, no two consecutive assistants), so one entry\n per assistant row is one entry per model turn.\n\n 2. ``auto_run_decision_receipts.manager_json`` → ``usage``. The autonomous\n (mission / auto-run) loop is driven by a mission manager that makes its\n own model call per decision. That call is billed but is NOT an assistant\n message: the manager's model is frequently a different one from the\n thread's, its duration is tens of seconds against the coding turns'\n minutes, and its usage matches no message row in any live store\n (verified: 42/42 unmatched). Skipping it undercounts every auto-run\n thread — 6.76M tokens, 2.35% of the capture.\n\n The SAME table also carries ``outcome_json.usage``, and that one is a\n duplicate: it restates the turn's final assistant message, byte for byte\n (verified: 37/37 matched an existing message row). Reading it would\n double-count every completed auto-run turn, so it is deliberately NOT\n read. Only the manager usage is taken.\n\n A receipt's own ``manager_json.model`` wins over ``threads.model``; 8 of 45\n live receipts disagree, and those would otherwise price at the wrong model.\n ``usage: {}`` (a cancelled or failed decision) is skipped, not zero-billed.\n\n metrics_json shape (all four fields observed on every usage row):\n {\"usage\": {\"inputTokens\", \"cachedInputTokens\", \"outputTokens\",\n \"reasoningOutputTokens\", \"totalTokens\"},\n \"context\": {...}, \"compactions\": [...], \"costUsd\": 0}\n\n Bucket conventions — BOTH verified across every row in four live stores\n (53/53 and 8/8):\n * ``inputTokens + outputTokens == totalTokens`` exactly. ``cachedInputTokens``\n is therefore a SUBSET of ``inputTokens`` (a cache-inclusive prompt, the\n ZCode/Qwen/WorkBuddy convention), so the cached share is split into its\n own bucket and billed at the cache rate.\n * ``reasoningOutputTokens <= outputTokens`` on every row that carries it.\n Reasoning is a SUBSET of output, and compute.py adds reasoning on top of\n output for display, so it is split out of output here (WorkBuddy rule).\n * ``cacheWrite`` is not persisted (zero by construction). Freebuff is a\n cloud service: the prompt cache is provider-side and read-only from the\n client's point of view, and no write counter exists in the store.\n * ``costUsd`` is present and always 0 on every observed row. Freebuff is\n NOT billed per token: a session buys an HOUR of a model with Freebucks\n (a daily allowance plus paid top-ups), and messages inside that hour are\n unlimited, so there is no per-token USD to record. ``costUsd`` is never\n read; cost is pricing-DB only, and it is an API-equivalent estimate\n rather than a bill. The authoritative Freebuff spend is the Freebucks\n burned on session admissions — a session-level ledger that is\n server-side only (nothing in ``desktop-v2.db`` carries a Freebucks or\n spend column, verified), so it is out of scope for this parser.\n\n Model attribution: ``threads.model`` is the thread's model and applies to\n every assistant row in it. It is stored in one of two forms:\n * a plain id (``z-ai/glm-5.3-flash``, ``deepseek-v4.1-flash``, ...),\n which the pricing DB resolves directly;\n * an opaque per-account handle of the form ``m-`` (e.g.\n ``m-22ff70c712``). The catalog mode mints these per account and they\n rotate; the mapping from handle to model is server-side and is never\n written to disk (the CLI comments this explicitly: \"a catalog carries\n handles, which are minted per account and rotate, so none of it is ever\n written to disk\"). A handle therefore cannot be resolved to a priced\n model offline and is carried verbatim, pricing at 0.00 exactly like a\n router alias absent from the DB (WorkBuddy ``default-model``, MiniMax\n ``MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`` precedent). The row still counts its tokens.\n This is the one documented accuracy gap for this source.\n\n The model id is split ONCE on \"/\" into (provider, model) so\n aggregate_entries composes ``provider/model`` without doubling the prefix\n (Muse/Qwen precedent); a handle carries no \"/\" and keeps provider \"\".\n\n Timestamps: ``messages.ts`` is epoch MILLISECONDS (verified against\n live rows: 1790924652181 → 2026-10-02). One entry per assistant row\n buckets that turn on the day it completed.\n\n Dedup: message entries key on ``freebuff::`` (``seq`` is\n the message table's AUTOINCREMENT primary key, stable for the row's life),\n and manager entries on ``freebuff::receipt:``. The\n two prefixes cannot collide — ``receipt:`` is not a valid ``seq`` — so a\n receipt whose id happens to be ``\"1\"`` never masquerades as message 1.\n\n The keys are source-global only because the thread id is unique across\n stores, and that is a property of the app, not of this parser: thread ids\n are ``crypto.randomUUID()`` (verified in the shipped bundle) and no live\n thread id appears in more than one project store (verified across four\n stores). A hypothetical build that copied a thread row between stores\n would collide on ``(source, entry_key)``, and the store's upsert would keep\n one — the same exposure every other thread-scoped source has.\n\n Storage mode: the store is WAL-mode and the desktop app keeps it open\n while running, so it is read through the shared copy-and-snapshot helper\n (zcode_snapshot) rather than opened in place — the live rows sit in the\n -wal, and a bare read-only open would both miss them and create sidecar\n state in the user's tree. Mode is file_replace: a thread's assistant rows\n are rewritten in place as turns complete, so each sync replaces the\n source's rows with the current values.\n\n Agent harness filtering: Freebuff Desktop supports multiple agent harnesses\n (``codebuff``, ``claude-code``, ``codex``). An unparseable date counts as open, so a bad value can only cost a\n recompute and never serves incomplete data.\n\n The comparison is on parsed dates, not on the strings: ``strptime`` accepts an\n unpadded ``2026-9-1``, which sorts after ``2026-10-01`` lexically and would keep a\n long-closed window recomputing every day.\n \"\"\"\n if not date_to:\n return True\n try:\n end = datetime.strptime(date_to, \"%Y-%m-%d\").date()\n except (TypeError, ValueError):\n return True\n return end >= _local_today()\n\n\ndef _day_scoped_key(base: str) -> str:\n \"\"\"Pin a key to the local day it was computed on.\"\"\"\n return f\"{base}_asof_{_local_today().isoformat()}\"\n\n\ndef _window_cache_key(base: str, date_from: Optional[str], date_to: Optional[str]) -> str:\n \"\"\"Pricing-aware cache key that also pins an OPEN window to its capture day.\n\n A day's usage is only complete once the day is over, and the response cache serves a\n stale entry with no upper bound on its age. The dashboard requests every quick range\n as an explicit date_from/date_to pair, so viewing \"Today\" on day D and clicking\n \"Yesterday\" on day D+1 build the same key: without this scope the second request is\n answered from the partial mid-day snapshot the first one left behind, and only the\n Refresh button (force_refresh) recomputes it.\n\n Stamping the capture day into open-window keys means a key WITHOUT the stamp can only\n have been filled after its window closed. Past ranges are therefore always complete,\n and stay cacheable indefinitely because their inputs no longer change.\n \"\"\"\n if _usage_window_is_open(date_from, date_to):\n base = _day_scoped_key(base)\n return _pricing_cache_key(base)\n\n\n# Keep only the latest signature per tool. A revision keeps large transcript\n# inventories out of cache keys and logs, without retaining every old inventory.\n_session_source_versions: dict[str, tuple[tuple, int]] = {}\n_session_source_versions_lock = threading.Lock()\n# These sources discover transcript trees; do not walk them in front of every\n# response-cache hit. Small fixed database inventories remain checked live.\n_SESSION_TREE_SOURCES = frozenset({\n \"codex\", \"claude\", \"pi_agent\", \"omp\", \"kimi\", \"dsh\", \"reasonix\",\n \"grok\", \"workbuddy\", \"qwen_code\", \"openclaw\", \"qoder_cli\", \"cline\",\n \"antigravity_cli\",\n})\n\n\ndef _session_source_revision(\n tool: str, *, force_refresh: bool = False, _startup_warm: bool = False\n) -> int:\n if tool in _SESSION_TREE_SOURCES and _SIG_TTL > 0:\n inventory_key = f\"session_source_inventory_{tool}\"\n warm_event = _begin_startup_warm(inventory_key) if _startup_warm else None\n try:\n signature = get_cached_or_fetch(\n inventory_key,\n lambda: session_source_signature(tool),\n force_refresh=force_refresh,\n ttl=_SIG_TTL,\n _startup_warm=_startup_warm,\n )\n finally:\n if warm_event is not None:\n _finish_startup_warm(inventory_key, warm_event)\n else:\n signature = session_source_signature(tool)\n with _session_source_versions_lock:\n previous = _session_source_versions.get(tool)\n if previous is not None and (previous[0] is signature or previous[0] == signature):\n _session_source_versions[tool] = (signature, previous[1])\n return previous[1]\n revision = 1 if previous is None else previous[1] + 1\n _session_source_versions[tool] = (signature, revision)\n return revision\n\n\ndef _session_response_cache_key(\n tool: str,\n period: str,\n date_from: Optional[str],\n date_to: Optional[str],\n include_review_sessions: Optional[bool],\n *,\n force_refresh: bool = False,\n _startup_warm: bool = False,\n) -> Optional[str]:\n tool = tool.strip().lower()\n try:\n revision = _session_source_revision(\n tool, force_refresh=force_refresh, _startup_warm=_startup_warm\n )\n except (OSError, sqlite3.Error):\n # Discovery can race a rotated/deleted file. Let the loader apply its\n # existing degradation rules, but never cache that response against an\n # incomplete inventory (nor let one unavailable tool abort warming).\n logger.warning(\"tokdash session signature unavailable tool=%s\", tool, exc_info=True)\n return None\n return _window_cache_key(\n f\"sessions_{tool}_{period}_{date_from}_{date_to}_{include_review_sessions}_source_{revision}\",\n date_from,\n date_to,\n )\n\n\ndef _active_time_cache_key(\n period: str,\n date_from: Optional[str],\n date_to: Optional[str],\n include_review_sessions: Optional[bool],\n) -> str:\n return _window_cache_key(\n f\"active_time_{period}_{date_from}_{date_to}_{include_review_sessions}\",\n date_from,\n date_to,\n )\n\n\ndef _active_time_payload(\n period: str,\n date_from: Optional[str],\n date_to: Optional[str],\n include_review_sessions: Optional[bool],\n) -> Any:\n \"\"\"What /api/active-time stores under its key — warmer and route alike.\n\n The route used to add ``range`` inside a closure no warmer could reach, so a\n warmed key held a payload one field short of the one a request builds. No\n caller reads that field on this endpoint today, which is precisely why the\n divergence would have sat there until one did.\n \"\"\"\n data = get_active_time_data(\n period, date_from, date_to, include_review_sessions=include_review_sessions\n )\n if isinstance(data, dict):\n data[\"range\"] = resolve_period(period, date_from, date_to)\n return data\n\n\ndef _usage_cache_key(period: str, date_from: Optional[str], date_to: Optional[str]) -> str:\n return _window_cache_key(f\"usage_{period}_{date_from}_{date_to}\", date_from, date_to)\n\n\ndef _insights_cache_key(\n period: str,\n date_from: Optional[str],\n date_to: Optional[str],\n facets: Optional[str],\n include_project_names: bool,\n) -> str:\n return _window_cache_key(\n f\"insights_{period}_{date_from}_{date_to}_{facets}_{include_project_names}\",\n date_from,\n date_to,\n )\n\n\ndef _warm_caches() -> None:\n \"\"\"Best-effort background warm so the first user request hits hot caches.\n\n Populates the parser caches (coding_tools._entry_cache, openclaw._ENTRY_CACHE)\n and the API response cache for the dashboard's initial loads — the exact Overview\n date range, Stats, each Sessions tool panel, and the Report tab's three windows.\n The period-only Today usage key is intentionally not warmed: the dashboard never\n requests it, and computing both forms used to duplicate the largest startup\n aggregation.\n\n The Report tab's share is the expensive half and goes last. Measured on one\n machine with a year of history: ~5s for the week, ~5s for the month and ~15s\n for the year, so roughly 25s on top of a ~22s base warm. The year window is\n most of it, and it scales with history rather than with the window. That is\n background CPU, but it is not free — it holds the interpreter lock in slices,\n so foreground requests during the warm are slower than they would otherwise\n be. TOKDASH_WARM_ON_START=0 turns the whole warm off.\n\n A foreground request for the key currently being warmed may join that one fill;\n see ``get_cached_or_fetch``. This keeps the browser's first load from racing the\n warmer into a transient 503 without relaxing the normal backpressure policy.\n Disable with TOKDASH_WARM_ON_START=0.\n Failures are swallowed; warming must never crash `serve`.\n \"\"\"\n # One clock for the whole list: read twice, a warm straddling local midnight\n # would build the Report keys for a different day than the Overview keys.\n day = _local_today()\n today = day.isoformat()\n # Composed by name, not by slicing _day_warm_targets(): the warm order is the order\n # the dashboard needs these in, and stats belongs second, immediately behind the\n # Overview usage key. Reordering the per-day targets must not silently demote it.\n def warmers():\n yield _usage_warm_target(today)\n yield (_window_cache_key(\"stats_None\", None, None), lambda: compute_stats(None))\n # Discover inventories only after the Overview and Stats have warmed.\n yield from _session_warm_targets(today)\n yield (_day_scoped_key(ACTIVITY_INSIGHTS_CACHE_KEY), get_codex_activity_insights)\n # Last: the heaviest warm, and the Overview is the tab that opens first.\n yield from _report_warm_targets(day)\n\n _run_warmers(warmers())\n\n\ndef _day_warm_targets(day: str) -> list:\n \"\"\"Every (key, fetch) pair the dashboard asks for with ``day`` as the whole range.\"\"\"\n return [_usage_warm_target(day), *_session_warm_targets(day)]\n\n\ndef _usage_warm_target(day: str):\n \"\"\"The Overview usage pair for ``day``.\n\n Mirror the dashboard exactly: its date picker sends an explicit date_from/date_to\n pair, not period=today. Building these through the same key helpers the routes use\n is what stops the warmer and the browser from drifting apart.\n \"\"\"\n return (\n _usage_cache_key(\"today\", day, day),\n lambda: compute_usage_with_comparison(\"today\", day, day),\n )\n\n\ndef _session_warm_targets(day: str) -> list:\n \"\"\"The per-tool Sessions pairs for ``day``, plus the cross-tool active time.\"\"\"\n targets: list = []\n for tool in SESSION_TOOLS:\n try:\n cache_key = _session_response_cache_key(\n tool, \"today\", day, day, None, _startup_warm=True\n )\n except CacheBackpressureError:\n # A foreground fill or a busy pool must not abort the other warmers.\n logger.debug(\"tokdash inventory warm deferred tool=%s\", tool)\n continue\n if cache_key is None:\n continue\n targets.append(\n (\n cache_key,\n lambda tool=tool: get_sessions_data(\n tool, \"today\", day, day, include_review_sessions=None\n ),\n )\n )\n targets.append(\n (\n _active_time_cache_key(\"today\", day, day, None),\n lambda: _active_time_payload(\"today\", day, day, None),\n )\n )\n return targets\n\n\n# The Report tab's facet request, verbatim (USAGE_REPORT_FACETS in index.html).\n# The facet string is part of the cache key, so a set listed in a different order\n# is a different key: the warm would fill one nobody asks for and the tab would\n# still pay the cold scan.\nREPORT_FACETS = \"daily,streaks,firsts,hourly,weekday,tools,models,projects\"\n\n\ndef _report_windows(day: date) -> list[tuple[str, str]]:\n \"\"\"The Report tab's three calendar-aligned windows, all ending on ``day``.\n\n Mirrors ``usageReportWindows()`` in index.html, Monday week start included.\n Cheapest first, so the light windows are ready while the year is still going.\n\n ``day`` is the *server's* local date, because that is what the cache key is\n stamped with. A reader whose browser sits in a different timezone can ask for\n a window a day either side of these and miss the warm entirely. That is\n correct rather than unfortunate — their window really is a different window —\n and it costs them one cold load, not a wrong number.\n \"\"\"\n return [\n ((day - timedelta(days=day.weekday())).isoformat(), day.isoformat()),\n (day.replace(day=1).isoformat(), day.isoformat()),\n (day.replace(month=1, day=1).isoformat(), day.isoformat()),\n ]\n\n\ndef _report_warm_targets(day: date, *, skip_single_day: bool = False) -> list:\n \"\"\"The three requests the Report tab issues, for each of its three windows.\n\n All three periods, because the tab restores the reader's last one from\n localStorage and the server cannot know which that was.\n\n ``skip_single_day`` drops any window that has collapsed to ``day`` alone —\n the week on a Monday, the month on the 1st. Only the midnight warm passes it;\n see ``_warm_report_windows`` for why the hour is what makes the difference.\n\n The tab sends no ``period`` parameter, so each key carries the *route's*\n default — \"today\" for usage and active time, \"year\" for insights — rather\n than the period the reader picked. Building them through the same helpers\n the routes use is what keeps that subtlety from silently un-warming this.\n Active time is also pinned to include_review_sessions=true here, which is a\n different key from the Overview's, and is why browsing the Overview never\n warmed this tab.\n \"\"\"\n targets: list = []\n for date_from, date_to in _report_windows(day):\n if skip_single_day and date_from == date_to:\n continue\n targets.append(\n (\n _usage_cache_key(\"today\", date_from, date_to),\n lambda f=date_from, t=date_to: compute_usage_with_comparison(\"today\", f, t),\n )\n )\n targets.append(\n (\n _insights_cache_key(\"year\", date_from, date_to, REPORT_FACETS, True),\n lambda f=date_from, t=date_to: compute_insights(\n \"year\", f, t, facets=REPORT_FACETS, include_project_names=True\n ),\n )\n )\n targets.append(\n (\n _active_time_cache_key(\"today\", date_from, date_to, True),\n lambda f=date_from, t=date_to: _active_time_payload(\"today\", f, t, True),\n )\n )\n return targets\n\n\ndef _run_warmers(warmers, *, join_seconds: Optional[float] = None) -> None:\n for key, fetch in warmers:\n warm_event = _begin_startup_warm(key, join_seconds)\n try:\n get_cached_or_fetch(key, fetch, _startup_warm=True)\n except Exception:\n pass\n finally:\n _finish_startup_warm(key, warm_event)\n\n\ndef _warm_previous_day() -> None:\n \"\"\"Warm the day that just ended, shortly after the local date rolls over.\n\n Every open-window key goes cold at midnight, and the day that just closed is the\n one the Yesterday button asks for all day. The join alone is reason\n # enough to shorten it: 10s-to-503 beats 30s-to-503 on a live server.\n _run_warmers(_day_warm_targets(yesterday), join_seconds=DAILY_WARM_JOIN_SECONDS)\n\n\ndef _warm_report_windows() -> None:\n \"\"\"Warm the Report tab's windows for the day that just started.\n\n A partial exception to the rule above. These windows end today, so they are\n open and go cold at midnight like every other open key — but a week, month or\n year at 00:05 is *usually* almost entirely days that have already closed, so\n the snapshot is worth having rather than near-empty.\n\n Usually, not always. On a Monday the week window is today alone, on the 1st\n the month window is, and on 1 January all three are. There the rule above\n applies unchanged: warming it would put the near-empty snapshot the Overview\n refuses to cache in front of the morning's first request, and this tab has no\n auto-refresh, so stale-while-revalidate would show an empty week until the\n reader loaded it a second time. A single-day window is also cheap to compute\n cold (a second or two), so skipping it costs the reader nothing.\n\n The startup warm keeps them: it runs when someone started the server, not at\n a fixed hour, so there is no near-empty window to protect against.\n\n Kept separate from ``_warm_previous_day`` rather than folded into it: that\n one warms a closed day and this one warms open windows, and the two docstrings\n would otherwise have to argue with each other.\n \"\"\"\n targets = _report_warm_targets(_local_today(), skip_single_day=True)\n _run_warmers(targets, join_seconds=DAILY_WARM_JOIN_SECONDS)\n\n\ndef _daily_warm_minute() -> int:\n \"\"\"Minutes past local midnight for the daily warm, default 5.\n\n ``0`` is a legitimate setting (warm exactly at midnight), so this cannot use\n ``_positive_int_env``, which would silently turn it back into the default. A value\n outside a day falls back to the default rather than wrapping into an unrelated time.\n \"\"\"\n minute = _non_negative_int_env(\"TOKDASH_DAILY_WARM_MINUTE\", _DEFAULT_DAILY_WARM_MINUTE)\n return minute if minute < 24 * 60 else _DEFAULT_DAILY_WARM_MINUTE\n\n\ndef _seconds_until_daily_warm(now: Optional[datetime] = None) -> float:\n \"\"\"Seconds until the next local warm time (default 00:05).\"\"\"\n current = now or datetime.now().astimezone()\n minute = _daily_warm_minute()\n target = current.replace(hour=0, minute=0, second=0, microsecond=0) + timedelta(minutes=minute)\n if target <= current:\n target += timedelta(days=1)\n return max(1.0, (target - current).total_seconds())\n\n\ndef _daily_warm_loop() -> None:\n while True:\n time.sleep(_seconds_until_daily_warm())\n try:\n _warm_previous_day()\n except Exception: # pragma: no cover - a warm failure must never kill the loop\n logger.debug(\"tokdash daily warm failed\", exc_info=True)\n try:\n _warm_report_windows()\n except Exception: # pragma: no cover - and neither half may kill the other\n logger.debug(\"tokdash daily report warm failed\", exc_info=True)\n\n\nasync def _warm_instance_identity() -> None:\n \"\"\"Background identity warm-up, swallowing nothing it could do anything about.\n\n ``get_instance_id_async`` already never raises for any data-dir problem and answers\n ``None`` instead, so the only thing this has to absorb is a cancellation at shutdown,\n which is normal and must not become a traceback on stderr.\n \"\"\"\n try:\n await get_instance_id_async()\n except asyncio.CancelledError: # pragma: no cover - shutdown race\n raise\n except Exception: # pragma: no cover - defensive, the accessor swallows OSError\n logger.warning(\"tokdash identity warm-up failed\", exc_info=True)\n\n\n@asynccontextmanager\nasync def _lifespan(app: \"FastAPI\"):\n # Fixture mode renders synthetic API payloads and must never start work against\n # real history in the background. Production behavior is unchanged unless the\n # explicit CLI switch set app.state.dev_fixture before uvicorn starts.\n if not _dev_fixture_mode(app) and os.environ.get(\"TOKDASH_WARM_ON_START\", \"1\") != \"0\":\n threading.Thread(target=_warm_caches, name=\"tokdash-warm\", daemon=True).start()\n if not _dev_fixture_mode(app) and os.environ.get(\"TOKDASH_DAILY_WARM\", \"1\") != \"0\":\n threading.Thread(target=_daily_warm_loop, name=\"tokdash-daily-warm\", daemon=True).start()\n # Warm the daemon identity alongside the other warm-ups, which is to say in the\n # background and never in front of the first request.
