The task is kept on the app so it cannot be\n # garbage-collected out from under itself, and cancelled on the way out so a daemon\n # shutting down in the first seconds of its life does not close the loop under it.\n app.state.identity_warm = asyncio.create_task(_warm_instance_identity())\n if not _dev_fixture_mode(app):\n # Boot-time reconciliation for the dashboard updater: an in-flight job whose\n # heartbeat went stale can never complete (its helper died with the outage or\n # the host rebooted), so it must not strand the UI in \"Updating…\" forever.\n # A fresh heartbeat means a live helper (e.g. a CLI update) and is left alone.\n try:\n from .onboard import update_jobs\n\n update_jobs.reconcile_boot()\n except Exception:\n pass\n try:\n yield\n finally:\n if not app.state.identity_warm.done():\n app.state.identity_warm.cancel()\n\n\n# No Swagger UI or ReDoc pages. FastAPI loads both from cdn.jsdelivr.net (pinned to a\n# major version only, no integrity check), and a script served on this origin can read\n# the write token from /api/csrf-token like the dashboard does. /openapi.json stays: it\n# is plain JSON with no third-party code, and API.md is the human-readable reference.\napp = FastAPI(\n title=\"Tokdash\",\n description=\"Local token & cost dashboard for AI coding tools\",\n version=__version__,\n lifespan=_lifespan,\n docs_url=None,\n redoc_url=None,\n contact={\"name\": \"Jingbiao Mei\"},\n license_info={\"name\": \"MIT\"},\n openapi_tags=[\n {\"name\": \"Pricing\", \"description\": \"Pricing database endpoints\"},\n {\"name\": \"Usage\", \"description\": \"Token usage and cost endpoints\"},\n {\"name\": \"Quota\", \"description\": \"Quota tracking and polling endpoints\"},\n {\"name\": \"Sessions\", \"description\": \"Session explorer endpoints\"},\n {\"name\": \"System\", \"description\": \"Health, version, and system endpoints\"},\n {\"name\": \"Updater\", \"description\": \"Click-to-update and managed install endpoints\"},\n ],\n)\n# follow_symlink=True: pipx/uv installs the packaged static assets as symlinks into\n# the uv cache. Traversal (\"..\") is still rejected via abspath.\napp.mount(\"/static\", StaticFiles(directory=str(STATIC_DIR), follow_symlink=True), name=\"static\")\napp.add_middleware(NoCacheMiddleware)\n\n\n# GUARDRAIL (issue #108): /health carries ``instance_id``, the value the dashboard uses\n# to tell one daemon behind several URLs from two daemons. Do not widen this policy to\n# make that field readable from a page that cannot read it. An unauthenticated\n# Access-Control-Allow-Origin would hand any website a durable tracking identifier for\n# this user. A route the browser is not allowed to read is shown as blocked instead.\ncors_allow_origins = [o.strip() for o in os.environ.get(\"TOKDASH_ALLOW_ORIGINS\", \"\").split(\",\") if o.strip()]\ncors_allow_origin_regex = os.environ.get(\"TOKDASH_ALLOW_ORIGIN_REGEX\", \"\").strip() or None\ncors_allow_same_tailnet = not cors_allow_origins and cors_allow_origin_regex is None\nif cors_allow_same_tailnet:\n cors_allow_origin_regex = r\"^https?://(localhost|127\\.0\\.0\\.1)(:\\d+)?$\"\n\napp.add_middleware(\n TailnetCORSMiddleware,\n allow_origins=cors_allow_origins,\n allow_origin_regex=cors_allow_origin_regex,\n allow_same_tailnet=cors_allow_same_tailnet,\n allow_credentials=False,\n allow_methods=[\"*\"],\n allow_headers=[\"*\"],\n)\napp.add_middleware(BasePathMiddleware, base_paths=SUPPORTED_BASE_PATHS)\n\n\n# --- Local write protection (Phase 0a) -------------------------------------------\n# The local API is unauthenticated, so every state-changing request must clear a gate\n# before it reaches a handler: the server must be bound to loopback, the Host (and any\n# Origin/Referer) must be a loopback address, and a per-process token must match. An `ssh -L` forward to localhost is deliberately different: it\n# preserves a loopback Host, so the SSH-authenticated user keeps write access by design\n# (SSH itself is the auth layer). With uvicorn --workers, each worker has its own\n# token; the dashboard fetches /api/csrf-token immediately before a write and browsers usually\n# reuse the same HTTP connection for the following PUT/POST. A client that gets a 403 after a\n# worker switch should fetch a new token and retry.\n_CSRF_TOKEN = secrets.token_urlsafe(32)\n_MUTATING_METHODS = {\"POST\", \"PUT\", \"PATCH\", \"DELETE\"}\n\n\ndef _is_loopback(addr: str) -> bool:\n addr = (addr or \"\").strip().lower()\n if addr == \"localhost\":\n return True\n # Strip brackets from IPv6 literals like \"[::1]\" before parsing.\n candidate = addr[1:-1] if addr.startswith(\"[\") and addr.endswith(\"]\") else addr\n try:\n # Parse as an IP so only the real 127.0.0.0/8 and ::1 loopback ranges match. A prefix\n # check like addr.startswith(\"127.\") would wrongly accept \"127.0.0.1.evil.com\".\n return ipaddress.ip_address(candidate).is_loopback\n except ValueError:\n return False\n\n\ndef _effective_bind() -> str:\n # serve() sets app.state before uvicorn.run; fall back to env, else \"\" (fail closed).\n return getattr(app.state, \"bind\", None) or os.environ.get(\"TOKDASH_HOST\", \"\")\n\n\ndef _effective_port() -> int:\n port = getattr(app.state, \"port\", None)\n if port:\n return int(port)\n try:\n return int(os.environ.get(\"TOKDASH_PORT\", \"55423\"))\n except ValueError:\n return 55423\n\n\ndef _host_allowlist(port: int) -> \"set[str]\":\n # The Host header carries no scheme, so this is netloc-only. The dashboard's own\n # requests always carry the explicit port (127.0.0.1:55423); a bare port-less Host is\n # legitimate ONLY when the server runs on :80 (Tokdash serves plain HTTP on loopback,\n # so :80 is the only implicit-port case). Adding bare forms unconditionally would let a\n # page served at http://localhost (:80) clear the gate (a real CSRF hole).\n allow: \"set[str]\" = set()\n for host in (\"127.0.0.1\", \"localhost\", \"[::1]\"):\n allow.add(f\"{host}:{port}\")\n if port == 80:\n allow.add(host)\n return allow\n\n\ndef _origin_allowlist(port: int) -> \"set[str]\":\n # Origin/Referer carry a scheme, so these are full origins and HTTP-only — comparing\n # netloc alone would accept https://localhost for an HTTP server on :80 (and vice\n # versa).
